response.sql: WITH rating_inventory AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(i.inventory_id) AS films_in_stock FROM inventory i JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), avg_across_ratings AS (SELECT AVG(films_in_stock) AS avg_count FROM rating_inventory), above_avg AS (SELECT ri.rating, ri.films_in_stock, aar.avg_count, ri.films_in_stock - aar.avg_count AS diff FROM rating_inventory ri CROSS JOIN avg_across_ratings aar WHERE ri.films_in_stock > aar.avg_count) SELECT SUM(films_in_stock) AS total_films_in_stock, AVG(diff) AS avg_above_average FROM above_avg

assumptions.assumption: "Films in stock" refers to the count of inventory items (physical copies) for each rating, not the count of distinct film titles. This metric is most relevant for inventory and revenue management.

alternatives.interpretation: "Films in stock" could refer to the count of distinct film titles available in each rating, rather than total inventory copies.
alternatives.sql: WITH rating_films AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT f.film_id) AS films_in_stock FROM inventory i JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), avg_across_ratings AS (SELECT AVG(films_in_stock) AS avg_count FROM rating_films), above_avg AS (SELECT rf.rating, rf.films_in_stock, aar.avg_count, rf.films_in_stock - aar.avg_count AS diff FROM rating_films rf CROSS JOIN avg_across_ratings aar WHERE rf.films_in_stock > aar.avg_count) SELECT SUM(films_in_stock) AS total_films_in_stock, AVG(diff) AS avg_above_average FROM above_avg
